questions.topic: Logic · deduction from a universal statement
questions.stem:
Consider this statement: Every chemist working in this laboratory speaks German.
Which of the following statements is deducible from the given statement?
options: Everyone in the laboratory who speaks German is a chemist.
Someone working in the laboratory who does not speak German is not one of its chemists.
Nobody in the laboratory speaks German.
Some chemists working in the laboratory do not speak German.
German is spoken in the laboratory only by chemists.
questions.exp: If every chemist in the laboratory speaks German, then anyone in the laboratory who lacks German cannot belong to that group of chemists, which is the contrapositive. The claim that everyone speaking German is a chemist is the converse, which does not follow, and the remaining options contradict or go beyond the given statement.

questions.stem:
From the given statements:
If the vaccine shipment arrives on Monday, then the clinic starts the vaccination campaign on Tuesday.
The campaign did not start on Tuesday.
Which conclusion can be deduced?
options: The vaccine shipment arrived on Monday.
The campaign will start on Wednesday.
The vaccine shipment did not arrive on Monday.
questions.exp: By modus tollens, if arriving on Monday would force a Tuesday start and there was no Tuesday start, the shipment cannot have arrived on Monday. Saying the shipment was lost goes beyond the premises, since a delay or a holiday closure would also be consistent with no Tuesday start.

questions.stem: Five runners, Ada, Beppe, Chiara, Dario and Elena, finished a race with no tied places. Dario finished before Chiara, Chiara finished before Ada, Ada finished before Beppe, and Beppe finished before Elena. Which of the following statements can be deduced?
questions.exp: The constraints chain into the single order Dario, Chiara, Ada, Beppe, Elena, so Elena is behind every runner who precedes Beppe, including Chiara. The other four statements each reverse one of the given relations.

questions.stem: Three friends, Nadia, Omar and Paolo, each drove home in a different car, one red, one blue and one white. Nadia drove neither the red nor the blue car, and Omar did not drive the blue car. Which of the following statements is true?
questions.exp: Nadia driving neither red nor blue forces her into the white car, and since Omar did not drive blue and white is taken, Omar drove red, leaving blue for Paolo. Every other option contradicts this unique assignment.

questions.stem: A watch gains 3 minutes every hour. It is set to the correct time at 8:00 am. When the true time is 10:00 am, the watch shows:
questions.exp: In the two hours since 8:00 am the watch has gained 2 × 3 = 6 minutes, so at a true time of 10:00 am it reads 10:06 am. The 10:03 option counts only one hour of gain, 9:57 am treats the watch as losing time, and 10:09 am triples the gain.

questions.stem:
Consider this statement: All squares are rectangles.
Which of the following statements is deducible from the given statement?
options: If a figure is not a rectangle, then it is not a square.
Every four-sided figure is a rectangle.
Squares and rectangles share no geometric properties.
questions.exp: The contrapositive of a universal statement follows with certainty: a figure outside the class of rectangles cannot be inside the subclass of squares. That all rectangles are squares is the invalid converse, and although some rectangles are indeed not squares in ordinary geometry, that fact is not deducible from the given statement alone, which makes it the trap here.

questions.stem:
From the given statements:
If it rains this afternoon, the tennis match will be moved indoors.
If the match is moved indoors, it will start at 2 pm.
The match did not start at 2 pm.
Which conclusion can be deduced?
options: The match was moved indoors but started at a different time.
It did not rain this afternoon.
questions.exp: No 2 pm start means, by modus tollens on the second statement, that the match was not moved indoors, and not being moved indoors in turn means, by modus tollens on the first statement, that it did not rain. Claims about lateness, cancellation or a delayed indoor start add information the premises do not contain.

questions.stem: Amara, Bruno and Chiara live on three different floors of a small building, one person per floor. Bruno lives on the third floor, Amara lives directly above Bruno, and Chiara lives directly above Amara. On which floor does Chiara live?
questions.exp: Bruno is fixed on the third floor, Amara directly above him is on the fourth, and Chiara directly above Amara is on the fifth. The other floors either duplicate Bruno's or place Chiara below her constraints.

questions.stem: Three students, Sara, Tom and Leo, each study exactly one foreign language among French, German and Spanish. Sara studies neither French nor German, and Leo studies German. Which of the following is correct?
questions.exp: Sara excluding French and German leaves her Spanish, and Leo already takes German, so the only language left for Tom is French. Each other option gives Tom or Sara a language already assigned or explicitly excluded.

questions.stem: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of an analogue clock at exactly 9:30?
questions.exp: At 9:30 the minute hand points at the 6, that is 180° round from the 12, while the hour hand has drifted halfway between the 9 and the 10, at 9.5 × 30° = 285°; the difference is 105°. The 90° option freezes the hour hand exactly on the 9 and ignores its half-hour drift.
